text:
Tanya H: Heads up — after the kernel-routing change from yesterday we're seeing a cluster of OOMs on rtx-pool-3 during KV-heavy chat workloads. Looks like fragmentation + small-chunk churn. Repro steps below.

Linh Nguyen: ugh. which knobs did you try so far? expandable_segments/max_split_size_mb/gc?

Tanya H: Quick notes: default config had expandable_segments=0, max_split_size_mb=32, garbage_collection_threshold=0.8. I flipped expandable_segments=1 and ran a 1h replay of the failing trace set. OOMs persisted but moved pattern: more frequent small-stalls before OOM.

Chris O: Can you paste the repro command and the tiny profiler snapshot?

Tanya H: repro command:
```bash
export REDWOOD_ALLOC_EXPANDABLE_SEGMENTS=1
export REDWOOD_ALLOC_MAX_SPLIT_SIZE_MB=32
export REDWOOD_GC_THRESHOLD=0.8
./tools/replay_trace --trace=kv-heavy-2026-03-10 --gpu-pool=rtx-pool-3 --concurrency=12
```
Profiler snippet (sample):
```
[2026-03-11 08:12:05] alloc: 24MB small-chunk @0x7f...  
[2026-03-11 08:12:05] free: 12MB  
[2026-03-11 08:12:05] grpc req batch=5 seq=128 kernel=optimized-attn -> workspace request 15MB
[2026-03-11 08:12:05] OOM when trying to allocate 64MB (no contiguous segment)
```
Linh Nguyen: That OOM on a 64MB contiguous alloc with expandable_segments=1 means max_split_size_mb is probably forcing a bunch of tiny segments that can't be coalesced. Can you try bumping max_split_size_mb to 64 and lower GC threshold to 0.6?

Tanya H: Did that quick test. With max_split_size_mb=64 & GC=0.6 the replay finished with 0 OOMs but latency p50 increased by ~8% (more GC scans). Concrete numbers: OOMs: 7 -> 0; p50 token latency: 12.1ms -> 13.1ms; p99 did not move.

Chris O: Useful signal. Sounds like two tradeoffs: larger split reduces fragmentation but increases headroom pressure and GC overhead. We should instrument contiguous-run length distribution and largest-free-seg telemetry.

dev-deploy-bot: deploy started: canary/kv-pool-rtx3-maxsplit64-gc06 (3 nodes)

Tanya H: Canary run is live. Also tried a micro-change: expandable_segments=0 + max_split_size_mb=64. That also finished without OOMs and lower p50 (12.3ms) vs expandable_segments=1 case. So expandable_segments behavior seems to interact poorly with our kernel-change batching pattern.

Linh Nguyen: Interesting — expandable_segments was supposed to help multi-size alloc requests, but if kernel routing now requests many small contiguous writes it may force internal fragmentation. We should add a quick unit that fuzzes allocation patterns (many small vs few large) and measure worst-case largest-free-chunk.

Chris O: Agreed. Action items:
- Tanya: capture contiguous-free-seg histogram for the failing traces and attach to the ticket (small CSV).
- Linh: add fuzz harness that emulates new kernel batching sequences (mix of 8-32 token windows) and run across 3 alloc knob combinations.
- SRE: watch canary for OOMs for 4h and escalate if >1 OOM/node.

sre-oncall: watching canary. Alerts set: OOM rate >0.2/min OR p50 token latency >20% baseline -> pager.

Tanya H: Quick trace histogram (excerpt): largest-free-seg-buckets: [0-16MB: 18%, 16-32MB: 41%, 32-64MB: 29%, 64-128MB: 8%, >128MB: 4%] — with default knobs. After max_split_size_mb=64 we saw >128MB bucket rise to 12%.

Linh Nguyen: Good. Preliminary hypothesis: kernel routing change increased short-lived KV cache churn which increases small free-fragment count; expandable_segments splits allocations and doesn't let bigger contiguous blocks form, causing medium-sized contiguous requests (>=64MB) to fail.

Chris O: Proposed mitigation for prod: roll max_split_size_mb to 64 on rtx-pool-3 and bump GC threshold down to 0.65 for a week to get more headroom and allow GC to be more aggressive, while we work on long-term allocator fixes (coalescing heuristics + defragmentation pass).

Tanya H: I'll open a perf ticket with the CSVs and push the fuzz harness PR by EOD. Also adding a quick runtime flag to log "largest_free_contig" on OOM so we'll have more signal next time.

dev-deploy-bot: canary/kv-pool-rtx3-maxsplit64-gc06 -> healthy nodes: 3/3

Linh Nguyen: Thanks. One more thing — add a regression test to CI that runs the 30s mini-replay under both allocator configs to ensure we don't re-introduce the pattern in future kernel changes.

Tanya H: Will do. tl;dr: temporary prod knob change (max_split_size_mb=64, gc=0.65) mitigates OOMs; root cause likely interplay between kernel routing and expandable_segments splitting semantics. Follow-ups: fuzz harness, contiguous-free telemetry, coalescing improvement RFC. :rocket:
